summary.headline: Anthem Biosciences Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose to INR594 crore with a 50.6% EBITDA margin; H1 revenue INR1,012 crore and net cash INR1,534 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue from operations was INR594 crore, with CRDMO at INR509 crore and Specialty Ingredients at INR85 crore. EBITDA was INR330 crore (50.6% margin, including INR59 crore other income) and PAT was INR211 crore (32.04% margin). Management attributed the margin uptick to operating leverage on a sharp revenue ramp after a weak Q1, with costs broadly flat. H1 FY27 revenue was INR1,012 crore, and an analyst noted an implied 7% H1 decline versus the prior year, which management did not dispute but addressed through a catch-up narrative for Q3 and Q4.

financial_highlights.change: Approx. 8% YoY as cited by an analyst; not confirmed by management
Other income INR59 crore vs INR48 crore in Q2 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR1,012 crore; CRDMO INR850 crore, Specialty Ingredients INR162 crore
financial_highlights.change: Analyst cited about 7% H1 de-growth; management did not dispute
Other income INR84 crore vs INR70 crore in H1 FY26

segments.name: CRDMO
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue INR509 crore; H1 FY27 INR850 crore. Around 85% of business is CDMO, of which about 65% is commercial manufacturing of approved molecules and the remaining about 20% is R&D and development supplies.

segments.name: Specialty Ingredients
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue INR85 crore; H1 FY27 INR162 crore. Management targets at least 20% of sales, and said the segment tends to be muted when CRDMO sales are strong.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to give a full-year revenue number but targets double-digit revenue growth, in line with historical delivery.

Management said it is confident of EBITDA and PAT growth, and expects FY26-level EBITDA margins (about 43% including other income) to be sustainable; the Q2 margin of about 50% was described as higher than this.
Catch-up expected in Q3 and Q4 to offset a weak Q1 FY27.
Specialty Ingredients expected at around 20% of sales by year end.
Capex guidance of about INR1,200 crore over two years for Unit 4 Phase 1 reaffirmed; Phase 2 is of similar size, with guidance to follow board approval.
Currency assumed range-bound (INR94.5 to INR96.5 per USD in the quarter), so no significant currency tailwind is assumed.
capex_capacity: Unit 4 is a large-scale facility on 30 acres; Phase 1 is equivalent to Units 1, 2 and 3 combined, with commissioning expected around March 2028.
Of the Phase 1 capex, management expects at least 30-35% in biology (fermentation/biologics) and the rest in chemistry.
Asset turns are currently about 1.2x-1.3x against an aspirational 1.5x; utilisation is below optimum and expected to improve over the next year.
Investments are underway in biologics drug product (fill-finish), oligonucleotides (Unit 4), an oncology facility expansion and cybersecurity.
demand_pricing: Portfolio: 15 commercial molecules (up from 14) and 9 late-stage molecules (down from 10); one molecule moved to commercial in Q2 on approval, from an emerging biotech portfolio in chronic care.

Geography: about 84% of revenue is international and about 16% India. Within international, US is about 22-24%, Europe about 60%, and rest of world 1-2%; customers are large pharma and the company says this split reflects where drug product is made.
Concentration: top five customers about 50% of business and top 10 about 80%.
Procurement: about 75-78% domestic on H1 basis, China about 20-21%, down from earlier reliance on a Chinese vendor for one product.

Five newly commercial molecules (last 18 months) split equally between APIs and advanced intermediates; management says the company is currently sole supplier, with second-source risk expected after acquisitions.
Management says it is seeing more RFPs and RFQs over the last quarter, though biotech funding revival is mixed given geopolitical uncertainty.
Company works with 8-9 large pharma customers, and two came in directly rather than via acquisition.
Peak sales estimates of the new molecules range from $1bn to $5bn, around $10bn aggregate, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin rose about 3%; is this due to lower China reliance?
qa_highlights.answer: Gawir Baig said the mix reflects reduced China sourcing, in-house manufacturing and product/customer mix differences, with no single driver isolated.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainability of the 50% EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 was driven by operating leverage on higher revenue with flat costs; FY26-level margins (about 43%) are sustainable, and management avoided committing to 50%.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year FY27 growth construct?
qa_highlights.answer: No full-year number given; management targets double-digit growth and expects catch-up in Q3 and Q4 after a low Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Timing of late-stage molecules moving to commercial?
qa_highlights.answer: Outcomes are expected over the next 18-24 months, with a few possibly in FY27, dependent on Phase III results; management said timing is not controllable.

qa_highlights.question: Prospects of the newly commercial molecule in the portfolio?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose indication details or peak sales, citing contract confidentiality; it described the indication as chronic care.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue per molecule for new vs older products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said on average per-molecule revenue should be similar to the existing base, with some large-indication molecules expected to exceed that; approvals for additional indications are expected in the next two quarters for some molecules.

qa_highlights.question: Why limited lateral (second-source) contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said customers have many qualified suppliers and switching is slow; the company is receiving samples and qualification work, which it sees as a positive.

risks_watch: Lumpiness of CRDMO project revenue: H1 revenue was down about 7% YoY per an analyst, with Q1 weak and reliance on Q3/Q4 catch-up.
Customer concentration: top 10 customers about 80% of business.
Patent expiries: first key patent expiry in 2032, with some extending to 2037-2040.
Late-stage pipeline (9 molecules) binary Phase III outcomes; 18-24 month commercialisation window.
Capex execution on Unit 4 (about INR1,200 crore Phase 1, commissioning around March 2028) and asset turn improvement from 1.2-1.3x toward 1.5x.
Residual China dependence (about 20-21% of procurement) and development of domestic captive vendors.
Biotech funding environment described as mixed amid geopolitical uncertainty.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and capex, with management repeatedly saying Q2 margins are sustainable. Cautious and at times evasive on forward numbers: it declined to give full-year revenue guidance, peak sales, molecule details, or Phase 2 capex, and framed timelines as dependent on customers and trial outcomes.
key_quotes: We have further solidified our industry -leading margins and are well -positioned to sustain this performance for the whole year.
Our customers do depend on us to pro vide a very competitive cost of goods. That's only possible if we are backward integrated.
So, historically, what we have delivered in the past, we will be able to deliver on those numbers.

adds.what: Unit 4 Phase 1 large-scale facility (30 acres), equivalent to Units 1, 2 and 3 combined

growth.why: Management targets double-digit full-year CRDMO growth (not quantified) and reaffirms ~INR1,200 crore Unit 4 Phase 1 capex with commissioning around March 2028, but gives no full-year number and H1 revenue implied a ~7% decline, so backing is partial.
